body.html: Moxy Bangkok Ratchaprasong opened in March 2024 as the first Moxy in Thailand — and also the largest Moxy in Asia Pacific, with 504 rooms across a tower at 111 Ratchadamri Road. In practical terms this address means the hotel sits directly above Big C Ratchadamri supermarket, linked by the covered R-Walk elevated walkway to CentralWorld mall and onward to BTS Chit Lom station — the whole journey under cover, out of Bangkok's sun and rain. For anyone staying here because of Police General Hospital, the route from the hotel is straightforward: walk north along Ratchadamri Road through the Ratchaprasong intersection to the hospital at 492/1 Rama I Road, roughly 700 metres or nine minutes on foot.

Moxy's design language is deliberately compact and social rather than spacious and private. The 504 rooms break down into standard Moxy Queen and Twin rooms at roughly 18–20 sqm, Corner Queen and Twin rooms at around 26 sqm, a Moxy Deluxe at 36 sqm, and a Loft option for families. Multiple reviews flag the standard room size as genuinely small — hooks cover every wall to compensate for minimal storage furniture, the in-room fridge is a compact mini-bar, and there is no work desk. What the rooms do have is a quality walk-in shower, city views, and the reliably fresh feel of a hotel that opened just over a year ago. The honest caveat on the shower is consistent across reviews: there is no curtain or screen, and without care the entire bathroom floor gets wet.

"Perfect location — I could walk to CentralWorld for dinner and Big C for supplies in the morning before going to the hospital. Staff were genuinely warm. Rooms are tiny though; go straight for the Deluxe if you're staying more than a night."

Where Moxy genuinely earns its higher review scores is in its communal spaces. The Social Hub on floor 9 is a proper communal hub — pool table, foosball, air hockey, a library corner, co-working desks, and the Moxy Bar running all day with food and cocktails. Staff regularly host evening events here: live music, games nights, and cocktail tutorials. None of this is found in a comparable mid-market hotel at this address. The Sato San Rooftop Bar on the 32nd floor takes a different mood entirely — it serves Thai-Isaan and Japanese-inspired food and cocktails against an unobstructed Bangkok skyline that several reviews describe as one of the best views in Ratchaprasong. The 24-hour gym consistently receives praise for its equipment range and availability.

The breakfast buffet draws broadly positive comments — fresh tropical fruit, congee, rice bowl stations, a full English spread, pastries, and Asian sides — and the à la carte hot-dish option lets guests order individual plates rather than heap the buffet. The main recurring complaint is the music volume: pumped-up pop plays in the restaurant, bar, and the lifts, which several guests on medical visits explicitly noted felt out of place. There is no swimming pool, cited by many reviewers as the clearest gap in the facilities for a 4-star city hotel at this price point. The small lifts can also feel congested at check-in and checkout peaks.

On balance, Moxy Bangkok Ratchaprasong is the best choice in this roundup for anyone who wants the newest hotel, the most convenient daily shopping, and an energetic atmosphere — and who is prepared to trade room space and quiet for those advantages. For patient families keeping a bedside vigil over many nights, the compact rooms and social-buzzing ambience may grate; in that case the Arnoma Grand or the Holiday Inn Bangkok on Ploenchit Road are quieter options that are closer to Police General Hospital. But for outpatients attending a short-term appointment series who want something fresh, walkable, and full of food options at arm's reach, the Moxy's score of 8.9 from nearly 1,900 reviews reflects what it does very well.

Practical notes from reading through the reviews: book the Deluxe (36 sqm) over the standard Queen or Twin if you are staying two nights or more — the jump in space genuinely changes the experience. Check-in takes place on floor 9 at the Social Hub, not at street level; first-time guests sometimes arrive confused at the ground-floor lobby. Request a room facing away from Ratchadamri Road if traffic noise concerns you. And use the R-Walk rather than walking at street level: it keeps you sheltered, connects directly to CentralWorld, and brings you to the BTS Chit Lom platform without crossing a single road.

honestSummary: Moxy Bangkok Ratchaprasong is the newest, freshest 4-star option in Ratchaprasong, with one of the best addresses in central Bangkok — Big C below, CentralWorld and BTS Chit Lom on the R-Walk, Police General Hospital nine minutes on foot. The trade-off is genuinely small standard rooms and a lively, music-heavy atmosphere that suits some guests and not others.
honestChecks: If you need space and plan to stay several nights — the standard 18–20 sqm rooms are too small for comfortable multi-night living with luggage → book the Deluxe (36 sqm) instead; the price difference is modest but the gain in comfort is significant

If you are here for a stressful medical reason and need quiet — Moxy's social-buzzing, music-heavy atmosphere is a real mismatch → consider Arnoma Grand (closer, quieter, pool) or Holiday Inn Bangkok on Ploenchit (closer still, more conventional)

If fresh facilities, walkable convenience, and good food access matter most — this is the strongest 4-star choice in the neighbourhood for those criteria → book the Deluxe early; peak-season (November–January) rates fill up fast

tips.title: Book the Deluxe for stays of 2+ nights
tips.body: The standard Queen or Twin rooms (18 sqm) feel cramped the moment you open two large bags. The Deluxe at 36 sqm costs a modest premium but changes the stay significantly — worth it for anyone here for several days of medical appointments or family support.

tips.title: Walking route to Police General Hospital
tips.body: From the hotel, walk north along Ratchadamri Road, through the Ratchaprasong intersection past the front of CentralWorld, and continue to 492/1 Rama I Road — Police General Hospital is on your left, approximately 700 m or 9 minutes. Easiest in the early morning before heat and traffic build.

tips.title: Big C is literally downstairs
tips.body: Big C Ratchadamri occupies the lower floors of the same building. Stock up on medicines, fruit, snacks, water, and household supplies without stepping outside — a genuine practical advantage for anyone buying daily supplies for a hospital patient.

tips.title: Use the R-Walk to BTS Chit Lom — no street crossing needed
tips.body: The covered R-Walk elevated walkway links the hotel to CentralWorld and the BTS Chit Lom platform without a single road crossing. From BTS Chit Lom you can reach Siam, Asok, Silom, and most of central Bangkok quickly even during peak-hour traffic.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Moxy Bangkok Ratchaprasong

faq.q: Where is Moxy Bangkok Ratchaprasong located, and how do I get there?
faq.a: The hotel is at 111 Ratchadamri Road, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok 10330, above Big C Ratchadamri supermarket. The easiest way to arrive is by BTS: take the Sukhumvit Line to Chit Lom station, then follow the R-Walk elevated walkway to the hotel — the whole walk takes about 5–6 minutes and stays under cover. From Suvarnabhumi Airport allow roughly 45–60 minutes by car or the Airport Rail Link plus BTS combination.

faq.q: How far is Moxy Bangkok Ratchaprasong from Police General Hospital?
faq.a: Police General Hospital (492/1 Rama I Road) is approximately 700 metres from the hotel — about a 9-minute walk. From the hotel, head north along Ratchadamri Road, pass through the Ratchaprasong intersection in front of CentralWorld, and continue to the hospital entrance on your left. The walk is straightforward and mostly flat; aim for early morning before the heat and pedestrian traffic build up.

faq.q: What are the room types and prices at Moxy Bangkok?
faq.a: Standard Moxy Queen and Twin rooms (18–20 sqm) start from approx. ฿2,900/night in low season. Corner rooms (26 sqm) run around ฿3,400, the Moxy Deluxe (36 sqm) around ฿3,900, and the Moxy Loft from around ฿4,500. During peak season (November–January) and long weekends rates rise considerably. Always compare across Agoda, Booking.com, and Trip.com before confirming.

faq.q: Does Moxy Bangkok Ratchaprasong have a swimming pool?
faq.a: No, there is no swimming pool. The hotel offers a 24-hour fully-equipped gym as its main fitness facility, plus the Social Hub games lounge on floor 9 and the Sato San Rooftop Bar on floor 32 for evening views. If a pool is a priority, consider the Arnoma Grand Bangkok nearby, which has both an outdoor and an indoor pool and is closer to Police General Hospital.

faq.q: Is Moxy Bangkok Ratchaprasong a good choice for patient families visiting Police General Hospital?
faq.a: It depends on your priorities. The location and in-building convenience (Big C supermarket, pharmacy, food) are genuinely excellent for anyone making daily trips to the hospital. However, the standard rooms are very compact and the hotel has a lively, music-heavy social atmosphere that does not suit everyone coming for medical reasons. For families needing more space or a quieter environment, Arnoma Grand (closer, pool) or Holiday Inn Bangkok on Ploenchit (closest 4-star) are worth comparing.
